expert.name: Lim Hui Fen
expert.employer_context: Keppel REIT Singapore Grade A office portfolio

TE-01.quote: First notice goes out within thirty minutes, full stop — and only to the tenants actually affected, not the whole building. It says what happened, where, what we're doing about it, when the next update is, and a contact number. No cause, no liability, no promise of a fix time. And it does not go out without a named human approving it — me or my delegate. I'm not having an automated message sent to a tenant on its own.

TE-02.quote: Tenants always ask 'when will it be fixed?'. You cannot answer that until the source is confirmed and isolation is done. I've seen a colleague promise two hours and it took six because the riser joint was worse than expected. So you say: our team is on site working to isolate the source, and we will provide an update on the repair timeline at the next update. You give them the next update time, not a completion time.

TE-03.quote: Do not tell the tenant what caused it until someone has actually confirmed it. Not 'appears to be', not 'we believe'. If the technician hasn't laid eyes on it and told you, you say the investigation is ongoing. The moment you say 'a pipe burst' and it turns out to be the sprinkler line, you've handed the tenant ammunition for a claim. Wait for Technical Services or the LEW to confirm.

TE-04.quote: A bank anchor tenant — or any tenant with a notification SLA in their lease — gets a phone call from the account manager within thirty minutes. Not the technician, not the Duty Manager, and not just an email. The account manager picks up the phone, then the written notice follows. The bank's facilities director needs to hear a human voice, not a template, when their trading floor is at risk.

TE-05.quote: PII, PDPA — you cannot put Tenant B's name in Tenant A's notice, and you cannot CC multiple tenants on one email. Each tenant gets their own notice. Unit numbers, individual names, contact details are masked in anything visible to a lower role. Lease terms and rental rates never go in any message. I had a junior put three tenants on one chain and we got a PDPA complaint — never again.

TE-06.quote: Data-centre clients are different. They don't get tenant-experience messages. The critical facilities manager handles the SLA notification — event reference, impact assessment, resolution window if you have one. The CFM approves it, not me. Different template, different channel, different approver. If you send a standard tenant notice to a hyperscale client, their legal team is on the phone before you've finished typing.

TE-07.quote: If the FSM or the FCC calls an evacuation or a stay-put, that goes out immediately over the PA and mass notification. It doesn't wait for me — the FSM has the authority, not Tenant Experience. What I do is log it and follow up with a written notice, and that written notice still goes through approval like any other.
